findings.evidence: Lines 51–52 say this proves a roadmap application “in Layer 4”; the documentation rubric explicitly excludes roadmap targets and layer numbers from module docstrings.
findings.fix: Remove the Layer 4 roadmap sentence/link; retain the mathematical Isaacs reference and keep roadmap attribution in the PR description.
findings.issue: The module docstring embeds roadmap-layer attribution, which is project-process metadata that will become stale when the roadmap is reorganized.

findings.evidence: Theorem `sum_eq_zero_or_norm_sum_eq_card_of_isIntegral` takes only `hn`, `hs`, and `hint`, while `isIntegral_character_div_finrank` takes and uses the `Nat.Coprime` hypothesis.
findings.fix: Say that coprimality supplies integrality of the average, after which the Kronecker lemma yields the dichotomy.
findings.issue: The docstring incorrectly says the roots-of-unity/Kronecker lemma is where coprimality is spent, although that lemma has no coprimality hypothesis; coprimality is used in the preceding Bézout integrality theorem.

findings.evidence: Lines 26–27 make the universal interval claim; `d = 1` is an immediate counterexample.
findings.fix: Replace this with the accurate weaker statement that intermediate absolute values can occur, or that the usual bound alone does not force the dichotomy.
findings.issue: The claim that an unrestricted sum of `d` roots of unity can have “any absolute value” in `[0,d]` is false: roots of unity form a countable set, so their finite sums cannot realize every value in an uncountable interval (and for `d = 1` the norm is always `1`).

findings.evidence: Complex.lean lines 39–40 call it the arithmetic half, while Vanishing.lean lines 22–34 label Bézout integrality the arithmetic half and this result the Kronecker half.
findings.fix: Describe it consistently as the Kronecker/analytic dichotomy used after the arithmetic integrality step.
findings.issue: The reference calls this roots-of-unity/Kronecker result the “arithmetic half,” conflicting with the other module’s description of it as the Kronecker half and of the Bézout integrality argument as the arithmetic half.

summary: The module documentation contains prohibited roadmap metadata and several inaccurate mathematical claims.
